verses.commentary: Cows of Bashan. The wealthy women of Samaria compared to well-fed cattle from the rich pastures of Bashan. They oppress the poor indirectly, demanding luxury from husbands who must exploit others to provide it. Bring us drinks! Complicity in oppression.
The Lord swears by his holiness. The most solemn oath. You will be taken away with hooks. Like fish caught and dragged, like cattle led by nose rings. The pampered become prisoners.

Straight out through breaches in the wall. No time to gather belongings. Through the gaps torn by invaders. Cast out toward Harmon, likely a place of exile or slaughter. The location uncertain, the fate clear.

Go to Bethel and sin. Biting sarcasm. The great shrines where they worship are places of rebellion. Every morning, every three years. More frequent than required. Zealous religion that misses God entirely.
Burn leavened bread, brag about freewill offerings. Technically incorrect offerings combined with public boasting. They love to announce their gifts. Religion as performance, worship as self-display.
I gave you empty stomachs. The first warning: famine. God's discipline through lack. Yet you have not returned to me. The refrain that structures the chapter. Warning given, warning ignored.
I withheld rain. Drought targeted and selective. One town rained on, another not. One field watered, another parched. God's precision in discipline. Impossible to dismiss as natural cycles.
People staggered from town to town for water. Desperate migration for survival. Yet you have not returned to me. The refrain repeats. Water crisis did not produce spiritual revival.
Blight and mildew destroyed gardens and vineyards. Locusts devoured figs and olives. Agricultural disaster. Yet you have not returned to me. Third refrain. Crop failure as divine speech, unheard.

Plagues like Egypt. Death of young men in war. Captured horses, stench of corpses. Egypt's plagues on Egypt's redeemed. Yet you have not returned to me. Fourth refrain. Even Egypt's judgment did not teach.

Overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah. Some survived barely, like a stick snatched from fire. Yet you have not returned to me. Fifth and final refrain. Even Sodom's fate, narrowly escaped, produced no turning.
Therefore this is what I will do. The content left unstated, terrifying in vagueness. Prepare to meet your God. Meeting God as enemy, not friend. Encounter with the Judge, not the Savior.

He forms mountains, creates wind, reveals thoughts. The creator hymn. God who shapes terrain and atmosphere also knows the mind. Dawn to darkness, heights of earth. The Lord God Almighty is his name. The one they must meet is omnipotent.
